sections.h2: How do I sell my house fast in Deptford, NJ?
sections.html:
You have three real routes: list the house with an agent, sell it yourself, or take a direct cash offer from a buyer. Deptford homeowners usually pick based on condition and calendar. A clean house with time to spare does well on the open market, while a house with deferred repairs, tenants, an estate attached, or a payoff date approaching often fits a direct sale better.

Deptford Township had an estimated 32,600 residents on July 1, 2025, up from 31,977 at the 2020 count. What slows a sale is often the paperwork and the condition of the house, so the sections below walk through the township's own offices, the Gloucester County Clerk, and the state forms that travel with every deed.

  • List with an agent: widest exposure, showings, and a buyer who usually needs a mortgage and an appraisal.
  • Sell it yourself: you keep the commission line, but you handle pricing, disclosures, and the buyer's attorney review.
  • Cash offer as-is: no showings and no repair list, with the price reflecting the work the buyer takes on.

sections.h2: What should I know about Deptford before I price a house here?
sections.html:
Deptford is a southeastern suburb of Philadelphia, about 10 miles from the city on the New Jersey side of the Walt Whitman Bridge and roughly 50 miles northwest of Atlantic City. The township covers 17.33 square miles of land and borders Woodbury, Woodbury Heights, Wenonah, Westville, West Deptford, Washington Township and Mantua Township in Gloucester County, plus Bellmawr, Runnemede and Gloucester Township across the Camden County line.

The place is old. It was formed in 1695 as Bethlehem and incorporated as a township in 1798. Its best-known story is the 1793 balloon landing at the Clement Oak, the first hot air balloon landing in North America. Most of the housing, though, came with the post-war boom: the population went from about 7,300 in 1950 to nearly 17,900 in 1960 and passed 24,000 by 1970. Much of the housing dates from that boom, so a buyer's inspector will look closely at roofs, heating systems and wiring.

Neighborhood names matter to buyers. Oak Valley is a census-designated place of about 3,500 people inside the township, and the unincorporated communities include Almonesson, Good Intent, Lake Tract, Jericho, Hammond Heights, Westcottville and Woodbury Gardens.

sections.h2: How do Deptford's roads, transit and shopping affect a sale?
sections.html:
Access to Philadelphia is a selling point for Deptford. Routes 41, 42, 45, 47 and 55 all cross the township, and county routes 534, 544, 551 and 553 fill in the grid. The New Jersey Turnpike is reached at Exit 3 in Bellmawr and Runnemede, and a short 0.07-mile piece of Interstate 295 touches the township. NJ Transit buses on the 400, 401, 402, 408, 410 and 412 lines run to Philadelphia, with local service on the 455 and 463.

Deptford Mall, the largest mall in the South Jersey region at about 1.07 million square feet of leasable space, anchors the retail side, with strip malls, restaurants and a movie theater around it. Tall Pines State Preserve, a 111-acre park that opened in November 2015 as Gloucester County's first state park, sits on the border with Mantua Township.

As of 2010 the township had about 150 miles of road: roughly 99 municipal, 29 county, 19 state, and 3.4 under the Turnpike Authority.

Deptford Township Schools serves the whole township, from pre-kindergarten through grade 12, and had 3,942 students in the 2020-21 school year. The elementary schools are Good Intent, Lake Tract, Oak Valley and Shady Lane for grades 1 to 5, with Central Early Childhood Center and Pine Acres Early Childhood Center covering the youngest grades. Monongahela Middle School takes grades 6 to 8, and Deptford Township High School takes grades 9 to 12.

Gloucester County students can also apply to the Gloucester County Institute of Technology, a tuition-free vocational high school located in Deptford. Ask the district which of the four elementary schools your street feeds and give that answer to buyers early.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Deptford homes?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's 2020-2024 estimates show a township where three out of four households own their home and where the median owner-occupied home is valued at $277,100.

Median owner costs run $2,112 a month with a mortgage and $927 without one, against median rent of $1,661. Owners weighing whether to rent out an inherited house can set those figures side by side.

sections.h2: Does the 2021 tornado still matter when I sell?
sections.html:
It can. On September 1, 2021, an EF3 tornado with winds up to 150 miles per hour, spun off by the remnants of Hurricane Ida, hit Deptford and damaged more than 100 homes. A house that was repaired should have closed permits and final inspections on file. A house that was patched without permits, or never fully repaired, can stall a mortgage buyer at the appraisal or the inspection stage.

If your house has storm repairs of any kind, gather the permit numbers, contractor invoices and insurance paperwork before you list. The township construction office, at 1011 Cooper Street and open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., can be reached at (856) 845-5300 about open permits and final inspections. A buyer paying cash can take a house with unfinished work as-is, but the price will reflect it.

sections.h2: What local approvals does a Deptford sale need?
sections.html:
The township construction office accepts applications for a Housing Certificate of Occupancy. Ask that office, before you sign a contract, whether your sale needs a housing certificate and what the inspection covers, because the buyer's attorney will ask for it.

Rental owners have one more step. State law N.J.S.A. 46:8-28 requires landlords to register with the township clerk, and the clerk's page says an owner who has not registered can be fined up to $500. If you are selling a rented Deptford house, confirm the registration is current. The clerk's office phone is 856-686-2203.

sections.h2: What does it cost to sell a house in Deptford?
sections.html:
The state charges the seller a realty transfer fee when the deed is recorded, computed on a sliding scale per $500 of price. Running the state schedule on a sale at the Census median value of $277,100 gives a fee of roughly $1,536. At $350,000 it is about $2,105, and prices above $350,000 move to a higher schedule.

  • Realty transfer fee: seller pays at recording, with an affidavit (form RTF-1) needed whenever an exemption is claimed.
  • Recording: the Gloucester County Clerk adds a $20 indexing fee to any paper deed that arrives without its cover sheet.
  • Seller's tax form: a GIT/REP form signed at closing; New Jersey residents use the GIT/REP-3 residency certification, while nonresidents may owe a prepayment of at least 2 percent of the price.
  • Payoffs: any mortgage, lien or unpaid municipal charge comes out of proceeds.

Agent commissions are set by your listing agreement, so ask for the exact figure in writing before comparing a listing against a cash offer.

sections.h2: How is the deed recorded for a Deptford sale?
sections.html:
Deeds for Deptford go to the Gloucester County Clerk's Office. The clerk's land records page says every deed must include one of the GIT/REP forms, and the Record Room can be reached at 856-853-3230. The office also offers a free Property Fraud Alert that notifies you each time a document is recorded in your name, which is worth setting up after any sale or inheritance.

If you need a copy of your old deed, the clerk's page points owners to the online land records search, where a copy can be printed for free, and warns against mailers that charge $75 to $86 for the same thing.

sections.h2: When does a cash offer make sense for a Deptford house?
sections.html: A direct purchase makes sense when speed or condition outweighs the last few thousand dollars of price. Examples in Deptford include a house inherited from a parent that no one wants to repair, a rental with tenants who are leaving, a house with storm or age-related damage, or a mortgage that is falling behind. Request offers in writing, ask what closing costs the buyer pays, and compare the net number to your best listing estimate.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Deptford with repairs still needed?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners sell Deptford houses with worn roofs, old systems and storm damage every year. A buyer paying cash takes the house as-is and prices the work in, while a buyer using a mortgage may ask for repairs after the inspection or appraisal.

faqs.q: Who records the deed after a Deptford closing?
faqs.a: The Gloucester County Clerk's Office records it. The deed must carry a GIT/REP form, and paper filings without a cover sheet pick up a $20 indexing fee. The Record Room number is 856-853-3230.

faqs.q: How much is the realty transfer fee on a Deptford sale?
faqs.a: It depends on the price. Under the state's sliding schedule, a sale at the Census median value of $277,100 would owe about $1,536, and a $350,000 sale about $2,105. The seller pays it when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Does Deptford require an inspection before I sell?
faqs.a: Ask the township construction office at (856) 845-5300. It handles housing certificates of occupancy, and it can tell you whether your sale needs one and what the inspector checks.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a rental house in Deptford before selling?
faqs.a: Landlords must register with the township clerk under N.J.S.A. 46:8-28, and the clerk's page lists a fine of up to $500 for missing registration. Confirm yours is current so it does not surface in the buyer's attorney review.
